# Do intervening practice outcomes predict EdNet answers after a break?

Use the complete learner members among the first 32 MiB of the publisher's EdNet KT1 ZIP. Take the first 2,500 complete learner entries in archive order. The teachers and learners were not randomly sampled by this procedure. Hash the learner filename stem with SHA-256, take the first four bytes modulo 100. Buckets 0–59 fit, 60–69 select model settings, 70–79 screen and 80–99 are reserved without inflating their ZIP members. Read up to the first 160 chronological rows per learner for a bounded trace. Exclude the final bundle if that cutoff splits it. Use the publisher's question answer key, part, and first question tag as the primary skill. Treat a solving ID as a bundle: every question in it receives the same strictly prior history. A previous bundle becomes available only once its latest within-bundle presentation timestamp plus its elapsed time has passed strictly before the new bundle's earliest presentation. Exclude queries without a completed earlier practice. This conservative bound may omit available history. The released times were shifted by learner, so absolute date features are excluded.

Fit a base CatBoost using part, question, skill, previous outcomes and counts overall and per skill/question. A clock model adds log time since prior exposures, gap since last eligible bundle, and past correctness under recency weighting. A second component adds intervening practice count and accuracy since the last same-skill practice, and aptitude summaries for recent same-part/different-skill events in the eligible prefix. Fit a matched combined tree with both feature groups. The proposed predictor averages this combined tree with the upstream pyKT implementation of SAKT under the same availability cutoffs and first-tag representation. Compare with each tree and SAKT, and with SAKT blended separately with each component tree. For each blend select SAKT weight in {0,.25,.5,.75,1} on tuning learners. Use CatBoost 350 rounds, depth 6, learning rate .1; use SAKT 64-dimensional embeddings, four heads, one block, 16 most recent eligible events, Adam .001, up to five epochs. Select checkpoint by tuning loss. All reported probabilities and indices refer to the same current questions. Record micro NLL and paired learner-cluster bootstrap 95% simultaneous intervals. Advance only when improvement over every control exceeds .015 nats and all simultaneous lower bounds exceed zero. Report break-stratified sample sizes. The historical ASSIST2015 study uses another population, history representation and horizon. Its numeric losses do not constitute comparators for EdNet.
